prompt: A function $f$ has the values $f(0) = 5$, $f(1) = 10$, $f(2) = 20$, and $f(3) = 40$. What is the value of $f(5)$?
hint: Compare each output with the one before it. Decide whether the same amount is being added or the same factor is being multiplied.

hints.text: Compare each output with the one before it. Decide whether the same amount is being added or the same factor is being multiplied.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try a shorter table: $3, 6, 12$ doubles each step, so the next terms are $24$ and $48$. Confirm the constant ratio, then keep applying it — and count your steps on paper.
Each output is twice the previous one and $f(0) = 5$, so $f(x) = 5 \cdot 2^x$. Use that rule with $x = 5$, or keep doubling from $f(3) = 40$.

learningObjective: Identify an exponential pattern and extend it.
explanation: The ratios $\dfrac{10}{5}$, $\dfrac{20}{10}$ and $\dfrac{40}{20}$ all equal $2$, so the function is exponential with base $2$.
The starting value is $f(0) = 5$, so the rule is $f(x) = 5 \cdot 2^x$.
Substitute $x = 5$ into the rule to get $f(5) = 5 \cdot 2^5 = 5 \cdot 32 = 160$, so the value of $f(5)$ is $160$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Just keep doubling
steps: Each value is twice the one before it, since $5$, $10$, $20$, $40$ doubles every time.
Continue from $f(3) = 40$: one more doubling gives $f(4) = 80$.
A second doubling takes the value to $f(5) = 160$, which is the answer.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: The value $80$ is $f(4)$, one doubling short, and it is the most common wrong answer.
From $f(3)$ to $f(5)$ the input rises by $2$, so two doublings are needed, not one.
Write them out as $40 \to 80 \to 160$ to see that $f(5) = 160$.
